# Mail URL destructors pass weak-reference handles to the main-thread release helper

The two destructors pass seven stored weak-reference handles through NS_ReleaseOnMainThread using each member's forget() result. Actual declarations identify them as nsWeakPtr, and inspected setters/getters use weak-reference creation and referent lookup. The added comments state that the non-threadsafe weak-reference proxy belongs to the main thread; the source change delegates release through the existing helper instead of leaving those members to implicit destruction. This finding is bounded to these URL fields and calls. The paired Gecko helper and native thread behavior were not validated, and no crash cure or general weak-reference rule is claimed.

Scope: Mail URL ownership.
